A recast never replays audio cached under the old voice.
A speaker the casting does not know gets the declared neutral voice, never a guessed gender.

tasks.title: Render combat as a 3D battlefield with Gaussian splats, in Rust only
tasks.objective: On the TV a fight is rendered by a Rust/WebAssembly WebGL2 renderer with no JavaScript: a 3D battlefield (a Gaussian splat scene where one exists, otherwise the location's painted ground and backdrop), a tile grid with glow, full-body figure billboards on tiles, named camera shots with eased moves and impact shake, colour grade, tilt-shift and vignette, health and initiative plates, and a finishing-blow cinematic. It ports the needed parts of the owner's earlier PlayCanvas battle stage.
acceptance_json: A fight on the TV shows every combatant as a full-body figure on its own tile on a ground that matches the location, readable from across a room at 1920x1080.
Each turn the acting figure is unmistakable and the camera moves to it without jumping.
An attack plays in order: the roll, a lunge at the target, hit or miss, damage, health change; a kill plays the finishing-blow cinematic before the scene changes.
Figure positions are staging only and are labelled as such in code; no rule, range or outcome is decided in the browser.
With reduced motion requested, camera moves and shakes are replaced by cuts and fades.
A missing figure or ground image falls back to a portrait token or plain ground; never blank.
Side by side with reference frames 120-140 the battle reads as the same kind of scene.
The named outcome has actual source/build-bound evidence; unsupported, pending, failed and unperformed checks remain explicit.
verification_json: Native tests of the pure layout and camera planner with a controlled clock.
Real browser frame captures of a full fight at TV size, including the finishing blow.
Coordinator comparison against the reference frames.
